subject: DONE s323b: a DECLARED sub beats indirect-object syntax — the same call parsed two ways inside vs outside parens
description:
FIXED s323b (Pl/PExpr.pm).

SYMPTOM: `[ divide $stdtext => 4 ]` died with `Can't locate object method "divide" via package "$var = do {"val" && $val;};"` — a package name that is a chunk of source text (it was the string VALUE of $stdtext).  Text-Balanced 05_extmul.t: 0 ok -> 59 ok / 27 not ok.

CAUSE: PExpr's indirect-object pre-pass rewrites `WORD $sym ARGS` to `$sym->WORD(ARGS)` and had no notion of "this name is already a sub".  Perl resolves the bareword at COMPILE TIME and a known sub wins, so `divide $text => 4` is `divide($text, 4)`.  PCL agreed at statement level (a different route) and disagreed inside `( … )` / `[ … ]` — only the nested form reaches this pre-pass.  Same construct, two answers depending on nesting.

FIX: `next if $self->_is_known_callable($method_name, 1)` in the pre-pass.  The helper is factored out of `_bareword_subscript_autoquotes`, which already asked Perl's same compile-time question for bareword array subscripts.

THE BREAKING CASE, probed (feedback_probe_the_breaking_case): the first version used the UNQUALIFIED declared-sub list and broke `[ show $w ]` where `Widget::show` is a method — a sub declared in ANOTHER package is not visible as a bare word from main, so that really is indirect syntax.  Hence the SAME_PKG_ONLY flag.  Note the prototype table cannot answer a package-qualified question at all (keyed by bare name — `Widget::show` registers as `show`), so under the flag it is not consulted; that makes the guard conservative, and an IMPORTED sub used as an indirect method still parses as before.

VERIFIED: corpus emission IDENTICAL across 111 files; gate 125/4475; sweep 0 new / 0 fixed.  Guard: Pl/t/transpile-test-09.t "a declared sub beats indirect-object syntax (#190)", 7 rows.
